summary: PASSED — Overview tab is fully editable with autosave and safe migration; Camera/Lighting multi-selects with searchable options, removable chips, custom free-text, reorder and mobile bottom-sheet all work. All 20 required testIDs are present (ov-title, ov-client, ov-campaign, ov-goal, ov-target_audience, ov-key_message, ov-call_to_action, ov-references, ov-extra_notes, ov-duration, ov-platform, ov-aspect_ratio, ov-language, ov-crew_size, ov-visual_style, ov-mood, ov-editing_style, ov-music_style, ov-camera, ov-lighting + ov-{camera|lighting}-{search,opt-<value>,remove-<value>,chip-<value>,custom,custom-add,done}). Verified on the seeded project 'Solstice Perfume' (c73286507b42) on desktop 1280 and mobile 390, in Dark and Light themes, and in English + Italian.
critical_code_review_comments: components.tsx MultiSelect: outer Pressable modal background uses onPress={() => setOpen(false)} while inner Pressable calls e.stopPropagation?.() — works on web where a real DOM event is passed, but on native RN Pressable the event has no stopPropagation. Ok for web preview; on native the sheet may close when tapping inside. Consider using Modal + View + a separate backdrop Pressable to be RN-safe (components.tsx:243-291).

project/[id].tsx:319-327 — the one-time migration effect writes to store on first mount (persist({custom_camera_style: p.camera_style})) which causes the header to flash 'Unsaved -> Saved' on first open of old projects. Confirmed the behaviour matches the PRD note. Consider gating with a persisted `migrated_v2` flag so it truly runs once per project.

project/[id].tsx:432-450 EditableField uses focused ref + debounced fire + onBlur commit. Verified: focus is retained when typing 20 consecutive chars while autosave fires (activeElement stayed ov-goal). Good design.

components.tsx MultiSelect selected-list uses moveUp only (no moveDown). Spec says reorder — arrow-up is enough since combined with removing/re-adding an item lands it at the end, but a down arrow would be more discoverable.

React 19 warning in browser console: 'Accessing element.ref was removed in React 19' — comes from a third-party lib (likely react-native-draggable-flatlist / reanimated). Not blocking, but worth watching upstream.
